contract.provides: For every finite-output classical channel T with binary input and every full-support fixed prior pi, let K=A_0+A_1, Y_y=T_{y0}A_0+T_{y1}A_1, and q_y=(T pi)_y. For arbitrary positive A_0,A_1 on any common finite-dimensional quantum reference, sum_{y:q_y>0} D(Y_y || q_y K) <= eta(T,pi) sum_{i=0}^1 D(A_i || pi_i K), where eta(T,pi) is the scalar fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant. Scalar references give the matching lower bound, so allowing an arbitrary finite quantum reference does not change this fixed-prior constant.
contract.requires: Finite-output stochastic channel with input alphabet {0,1}; full-support fixed prior pi; arbitrary finite-dimensional positive operator weights A_0,A_1; omit zero output-prior symbols.

source_excerpts.text:
## Complete fixed-prior SDPI for a binary classical input

As a direct consequence, let T be any finite-output classical channel with TWO
input symbols and faithful fixed prior pi. Its fixed-prior scalar Umegaki SDPI
constant equals the constant after allowing arbitrary finite quantum reference:
for arbitrary positive A0,A1, K=A0+A1, Y_y=T_y0 A0+T_y1 A1,

sum_y Tr Y_y(logY_y-log((Tpi)_y K))
 <= eta(T,pi) sum_i Tr Ai(logAi-log(pi_i K)).

Zero output-prior symbols are omitted. The difference of the two sides is a
balanced two-source entropy combination plus linear trace terms, so the scalar
inequality lifts exactly by the theorem. Normalization is harmless by
homogeneity. Scalar references give the matching lower bound. This is fixed-
PRIOR, binary transmitted alphabet, arbitrary quantum-reference dimension; it
is different from the earlier arbitrary-alphabet/qubit-reference GLOBAL theorem.
No reduction of a general multi-symbol quantum-memory problem to binary symbols
is asserted.

25 October2026. The external governing theorem is Frenkel2023, arXiv2208.12194v4,
Theorem6, https://arxiv.org/html/2208.12194 . It gives Umegaki relative entropy via
signed-pencil negative traces, including unequal traces. The new receiving
construction forms the positive second-derivative measure of a binary testing
curve and applies that theorem to all positive mixtures. No physical measurement
or decoder equivalence follows. Historical priority of this direct consequence
has not been established by the bounded search.

source_excerpts.text:
Wang–Gohari2026, arXiv2610.29576v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29576v1 ,
Proposition5 already proves scalar/matrix equality for doubly symmetric binary
sources throughout its matrix-entropy class. The present Umegaki result covers
arbitrary binary-input finite-output channels at their fixed priors, by the exact
two-source transfer. It does NOT resolve that paper's general multi-symbol
matrix-entropy questions or manufacture a t log t SDPI separation from the
three-source trine trace-entropy counterexample.
